effects.name: ACNet
effects.summary: Convolutional neural network 2× amplification, mainly for animation materials and with strong noise reduction orientation.
effects.details:
Upscaling and super resolution › Anime and line art

Suitable for animations and line drawings with compression noise; relatively clean or real-life materials should be compared with models with stronger texture preservation.

Variant differences: fixed 2×; 9 calculation channels, strong noise reduction may lose fine textures, no native picture comparison.

Advanced/Experimental: Multi-channel or larger network models, suitable for comparison when there is performance margin.

First try: Check performance by target resolution; don't infer quality just by name

Combination guidance: Main scaling step; after "necessary denoising/restoration"; before "anti-aliasing, sharpening, display style". Let the size reconstruction be completed first, and then do the finishing touches related to the output resolution.

Output size: fixed magnification: width × 2, height × 2

Requirements: Direct3D 11 effects shaders are compilable; the target output size satisfies the file's size expression

Performance cost: medium to high; specific frame rate needs to be measured on the target screen.

Pairing recovery automatically uses upstream parameters; white point and exposure only apply to native SDR mapping. Maintain input dimensions.

Requirements: Output screen with Windows HDR enabled. Normal white point mapping does not produce highlight detail that is not present in the original footage. Recovery after SDR processing is not guaranteed to be lossless.

Advanced/Experimental: For customizing color workflows, first compare white points, gradients and highlights.

Performance cost: Adds one full-frame GPU conversion per process, cost scales with resolution. Parameter modifications take effect after rescaling.

HDR components

Placed after the SDR effect as an alternative to SDR → HDR. HDR input first passes through HDR → SDR; AI expansion will reshape brightness and color, which does not mean restoring the original HDR.

Requirements: NVIDIA RTX 20 series and newer graphics cards, available RTX Video HDR runtime library and driver, and Windows HDR enabled on the output screen. Maintain input dimensions.

Parameters: contrast, saturation, mid-grey and peak brightness. Peaking is set per target monitor. The frame-filling stage is entered only after the image effect is completed.

Advanced/Experimental: For customizing color workflows, first compare white points, gradients and highlights.

Performance cost: NVIDIA AI inference, actual overhead is determined by resolution and graphics card. The four parameters can be adjusted in real time in the toolbar and applied to subsequent processing frames.
